correctness.rationale: Writing n_i=1+y_i with sum y_i=r gives fixed-total Berger-Parker order by M=max y_i and Simpson order by Q=sum y_i^2. For fixed r and smaller maximum m, Q is at most floor(r/m)m^2+(r mod m)^2, while with larger maximum m′ it is at least m′^2+(r-m′); direct finite algebra check for every r<=7 and m<m′ ensures no opposite order. Independent partition generator (not package verifier) exhaustively found strict-reversal counts 0 through r=7 and four at r=8. Four explicitly listed partitions have maximum-coordinate versus sum-of-squares reversal. At k>=3 excess (1,2,5) vs (4,4) yields (2,3,6) vs (1,5,5), M=5>4 but Q=30<32; k-padding preserves both. Four types require 6,5,4,3 nonzero coordinates, giving 1,2,3,4 for increasing richness. Two shares p>=1/2 have p and p²+(1-p)² monotone, proving all N nonreversal at k=2. Finite-sample Simpson is fixed-total affine transform and retains ranking.

value.rationale: Berger-Parker and Simpson are natural, widely used indices; exact minimal integer resolution at which they induce opposite strict comparisons under controlled richness and total is a meaningful sampling-design boundary. The all-k theorem and full first-layer classification are genuine finite extremal results, not merely a numerical sample: a researcher deciding when discordance is combinatorially possible can use the precise k+8 threshold.

final_claim: At fixed richness k>=3, same total N and positive integer species counts, Berger-Parker dominance versus Simpson concentration cannot have opposite strict rankings when N-k<=7; eight excess individuals are necessary and sufficient. The first excess layer has 1,2,3,4 unlabeled reversing profile-pair types for k=3,4,5,k>=6. Two-species communities never reverse.
limitations: Same fixed richness, equal total abundance, strictly positive integers, Berger-Parker maximum and Simpson concentration orientation.
Existing ecological index formulas/qualitative differences are credited; unindexed finite example remains possible.
